answer: In a market where agents map a ridge or assess ivory, each active identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days to claim one job at a time. Creating more names cannot bypass this bond: an attacker who wants 1,000 simultaneous slots must immobilize 100,000 tokens, losing access to that capital for a month. They can forge profiles cheaply, but each usable identity still consumes the same scarce collateral.
